csv_project_name: AE Svc for St.Clair County International Airport FY 2026-31
csv_agency: St. Clair County International Airport - KPHN
csv_scope_of_work: St. Clair County International Airport Port Huron intends to select a consultant to assist in airport development projects. Interested consulting firms are requested to submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) in triplicate to Abby Terhune, Ste. 203, Port Huron, MI 48060 no later than 3:00 P.M. Monday, August 3rd, 2026. The SOQ should demonstrate the consultants interest in providing airport planning, architectural/engineering design, and construction administration services focused on St. Clair County International Airport s current Five-Year Airport Capital Improvement Plan (ACIP). Services will include general consulting and advisement on airport development issues including assistance in the following projects: Runway 04/22 Obstruction Removal Wetland Mitigation Runway 10/28 Obstruction Removal Environmental Assessment Terminal Building - Planning
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Civil Engineering, Construction/Project Management, Land Use Planning, Planning/Master Planning, Transportation Planning
csv_comments: '- Project Funding: Multiple grants- Solicitation documents available online.
title: AE Services for St. Clair County International Airport FY 2026-31
short_description: Consulting services for airport development, planning, design, and construction administration projects.
project_scope: Consultant support for airport development projects at St. Clair County International Airport under the current Five-Year Airport Capital Improvement Plan. Listed projects include Runway 04/22 obstruction removal, wetland mitigation, Runway 10/28 obstruction removal, environmental assessment, and terminal building planning.
services: Airport planning, architectural and engineering design, construction administration, general consulting and advisory services, architecture services, civil engineering, construction/project management, land use planning, planning/master planning, and transportation planning.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily an airport planning and general consulting assignment rather than a defined structural engineering project.
- Includes architecture and engineering design, but no specific bridge, long-span roof, special structure, or complex building scope is defined.
- Significant portions relate to obstruction removal, wetland mitigation, environmental assessment, and planning, which are not core sbp target services.
- Terminal building planning is mentioned, but only at a planning level without size, complexity, or structural ambition.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated in the source. The notice references multiple airport development projects funded by multiple grants, but provides no cost figures. A realistic estimate is not possible from the available information because project sizes, quantities, and implementation scope are not defined.
fee_explanation: No fee information is stated in the source. The procurement is for a consultant SOQ covering multiple possible airport development tasks over a 60-month period, so a realistic sbp fee estimate is not possible from the available information.
references_qualifications: Interested consulting firms must submit a Statement of Qualifications in triplicate demonstrating interest and capability to provide airport planning, architectural/engineering design, and construction administration services related to the airport's Five-Year ACIP.
award_criteria: Not specified in the source; selection is based on a Statement of Qualifications under an RFP/RFQ process.
contracting_authority: St. Clair County International Airport - KPHN, St. Clair County, Michigan. Location: Port Huron/Kimball, MI, USA. Contact: Catherine Fiore. Phone: 810-364-6890. Email: cfiore@stclaircounty.org. Website: https://www.michigan.gov/mdot/Travel/Mobility/Aeronautics/planning-development/advertisements
notes: Project #870011; ProjectID 1016365; DR #202600273336. Contract duration 60 months, non-renewable. Funding via multiple grants. Although terminal building planning is included, the tender is mainly a multi-disciplinary airport development consulting assignment and not a clearly defined building or structural project.
